PER-APP OAUTH 2.1 PROVIDER: every app with auth ALSO acts as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server on its own origin, so external MCP clients (Claude.ai connectors, ChatGPT connectors, Cursor) can authenticate an APP user without pasting raw tokens.

Endpoints (auto-mounted, zero config): GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server, GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/<path>], POST /oauth/register (RFC 7591 DCR), GET /oauth/authorize (PKCE S256 required; bounces anonymous users through the app's own /login?next=...; shows a consent page naming the client and redirect host) + POST /oauth/authorize (the user's same-origin Approve/Deny; only this issues a code, bound to the signed-in user and exact request by a 10-minute consent token), POST /oauth/token.

On legacy apps without mcp.yaml, minted access tokens are plain _benmore_api_tokens rows (name 'oauth: <client>', 30d expiry) holding the scope the user approved: a list of resource:action scopes (`notes:read tasks:write`) narrows the token to exactly those, and no scope, `*` or non-framework names (`openid`) grant full access, which the consent page then says - the normal Bearer path validates them, so any `auth: required` flow works as an OAuth-protected MCP tool with `${{ user.id }}` bound to the real user. Users list/revoke them via GET/DELETE /api/_auth/api-tokens.

401s from auth-required flows carry `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=...` (RFC 9728) so MCP clients discover the provider automatically. Ship an MCP endpoint as a flow (e.g. POST /api/mcp) with auth: required and point Claude's custom-connector UI at it - the OAuth dance happens with the APP's users, not platform accounts.
